description: A granulator: it takes short pieces out of a recording of the input and replays them, with control over their length, their pitch and where in the recording they come from.

params.text: How much random variation is added to the grain length.
How far each grain is pitched away from the recording.
How much random variation is added to that pitch.
Where in the recorded buffer the grains are taken from.
How much random variation is added to that position.
Sets how the buffer is read: up runs forwards, middle freezes the recording so the grains keep coming from the same material, down runs backwards.

inputs.text: Moves the read position, by as much as the MOD knob beside POS allows.
Moves the grain pitch, by as much as the MOD knob beside DETUNE allows.
A trigger that starts a grain. With nothing patched here grains follow one another continuously.
Moves the grain length, by as much as the MOD knob beside SIZE allows.
Audio recorded into the buffer the grains are taken from.
Sets where the grains are placed across the stereo outputs.

notes: Set Rack's sample rate to 96kHz before using this module. At any other rate it runs at the wrong speed, and a red bar appears across the bottom of the panel saying so.
An unpatched modulation CV jack does not read 0V: the firmware drives it from an internal chaotic generator, so a MOD knob turned up with nothing patched lets a wandering voltage through.
The TRIG jack starts a grain on a rising edge, but its threshold is so low that a patched signal must fall below about -4.9V to read as low again, so an ordinary gate fires once.
